selection_rationale: cand-2026-004 received a 'pass' review and best meets CNSM constraints: high reproducibility, feasible compute budget, strong venue relevance, and a concrete deliverable (public executable benchmark + harness) that aligns with the track's focus on action-level NetOps safety and evaluation. Other candidates required substantive design repairs (see runner-up) while cand-2026-004's remaining concerns are addressable before preregistration.
unresolved_uncertainties: Rollback emulation may oversimplify true operational rollback complexity and irreversible action semantics.
Representativeness of benchmark topologies and intents for real-world deployments (scale, vendor/OS diversity) is unclear.
Risk of benchmark overfitting or gaming by tuned pipelines absent anti-overfitting protocols (hidden test split, challenge rules).
Sensitivity of pipeline rankings to verifier fidelity and scoring-design choices (rollback-penalty weighting).
required_repairs_before_preregistration: Precisely define rollback semantics and document limitations of rollback emulation; include clear examples distinguishing reversible vs irreversible states.
Design and document anti-overfitting measures (hidden test split, challenge/evaluation protocol) and publish an evaluation harness with seed-controlled reruns and result verification.
Increase or justify topology and intent diversity; where possible include at least one realistic publicly sourced topology/intent trace and document representativeness rationale.
Formally specify scoring protocols (verifier-pass, action-impact, rollback-penalty-adjusted), enumerate edge cases, provide reference implementations, and publish artifact hashes for reproducibility.
